body:
mira: Heads-up — after flipping the incremental authz-mapping flag in canary, we saw ~4% of requests get attributed to the org fallback instead of project (sampled from canary region). Noticed during smoke runs around 11:32 UTC. logs: `authz: fallback_source=org reason=missing_project_claim user=svc-ingest`

sam: Ugh. Is that from token parsing or routing?

jordan: From quick grep it looks like the project claim is present upstream but gets dropped in the proxy when we rewrite `x-origin` header. possible header strip bug.

lee: Can you paste the raw header dump?

mira: snippet: `{"authorization":"Bearer ...","x-origin":"project:proj-42","x-service":"svc-ingest"}` then downstream shows `x-origin` missing. We only see `authorization` and `x-service`.

anita: ops-bot reported a spike in org-level quota usage because attribution fell back. Can we throttle canary so it doesn't trip global alerts? :eyes:

ops-bot: incident: quota-threshold-crossed for org:org-7 (90% of soft limit). Notifying billing/sre.

sam: Immediate plan: 1) pause the canary rollout in remaining regions 2) revert mapping flag in canary 3) add header-preservation test in proxy unit tests. Anyone object?

jordan: +1 to pause. Also propose adding a tagged telemetry event `authz.project_missing` with context (route, token_hash) so we can correlate.

lee: For the dashboard: add a small panel that shows project vs org attribution ratio over last 6h + a sampling of token fingerprints when fallback happens. That will help diagnose whether it's a specific client.

mira: Revert done in canary (rolled back at 11:46 UTC). ops-bot stopped firing after that.

anita: Thanks. For rollout safety, suggest feature-flag gating: require `x-origin` header to be preserved OR the proxy must extract project claim from token if header missing. We need explicit fallback policy in code and docs.

sam: Agreed. Also add a canary guard that stops rollout if org attribution increases >2% relative to baseline for 10m. Simple thresholding.

jordan: Implementation notes: we have two places to touch — (A) proxy header pass-through (B) mapping service that normalizes claims. I'll open two PRs. PR1 will add an e2e `curl -H \"x-origin: project:proj-42\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" $PROXY | jq .` and assert `x-origin` present downstream.

lee: Telemetry schema: new metric `redwood.authz.fallback_reason` label={reason, route, region} export to prometheus. Also log an event with `token_hash` and `project_claim` for 1% sampled requests. Keep PII out.

anita: Ops ask: can we backfill which customers hit the org fallback during the 14m window? We need to contact kevin (support) if any billing impact.

mira: I can run a query on request logs by time window and project attribution tag. Will share a CSV.

sam: Action items: sam -> add threshold guard + pause logic; jordan -> PRs for proxy tests + mapping service fix; lee -> dashboard panels + metric schema; mira -> log query CSV + follow-up with support; anita -> coordinate with SRE/billing on alerts.

lee: Quick UX note: in the console rollout flow, we should surface a warning next to the flag: \"This change may affect attribution/billing; enable in canary only and monitor project attribution dashboard.\" Small copy change avoids surprises.

mira: Good point. I'll file a tiny docs PR.

jordan: FYI I reproduced locally by running `make proxy-dev` and injecting a header-drop filter. Root cause seems to be the new header sanitization step misconfigured for prefixed headers. Fix ready, adding unit + integration tests.

sam: Great. Let's aim to re-rollout after tests + dashboard visible + guard in place. Target re-canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

anita: I'll schedule a brief 15m oncall check at 09:05 to watch alerts.

mira: Thanks all. Closing here but will post results of log query and PR links when ready. :white_check_mark:
